title: Molecular identification, quantification and phylogeny of non-polio enteroviruses: A wastewater-based epidemiology from northeastern Nigeria
abstract: Abstract Non-polio enteroviruses (NPEV) pose a major, potentially deadly global health threat. While most infections are mild or asymptomatic, certain strains cause severe complications, requiring enhanced clinical and environmental surveillance for effective management. This study utilised wastewater-based epidemiology to assess the extent of NPEV contamination across six northeastern states in Nigeria. We collected and processed 400 sewage water samples for virus isolation and identification using RD and L20B cell lines and qPCR, and genotyped them by Sanger sequencing. The overall prevalence of NPEVs was 42.3% and was significantly highest in Gombe state (55.4%, OR = 2.14, p = 0.0372). Remarkably, a high viral copy number of 4.28 ± 0.3 log10 was obtained at a sampling site in Adamawa State. Viral copy numbers differed significantly across sampling sites in all states ( p p > 0.05). Borno State had the highest mean NPEV copy numbers, followed by Taraba State, whose mean copy number was closely related to those of other states. Sequence analyses revealed genetic diversity among Echovirus E19 isolates from Borno and Yobe States. One Echovirus E19 isolate from Borno State clustered closely with another strain previously described in Ibadan, Nigeria. These findings reveal diverse and high levels of NPEV contamination in most sewage samples in northeastern Nigeria. Moreover, the relatedness of Echovirus E19 to one described over a decade ago in southwestern Nigeria highlights active local transmission and underscores the need for continuous NPEV surveillance across One Health niches.

abstract_zh: 摘要 非脊髓灰质炎肠道病毒(NPEV)是全球范围内具有潜在致命性的重大健康威胁。尽管大多数感染为轻度或无症状,但某些毒株会导致严重并发症,因此需要加强临床和环境监测以有效管理。本研究利用废水基流行病学方法,评估了尼日利亚东北部六个州的NPEV污染程度。我们收集并处理了400份污水样本,使用RD和L20B细胞系及qPCR进行病毒分离和鉴定,并通过Sanger测序进行基因分型。总体患病率为42.3%,其中戈姆贝州的患病率显著最高(55.4%,OR = 2.14,p = 0.0372)。令人惊讶的是,在阿达马瓦州的一个采样点获得了高达4.28 ± 0.3 log10的高病毒拷贝数。所有州的采样点间病毒拷贝数均存在显著差异(p > 0.05)。博尔诺州的NPEV平均拷贝数最高,其次是塔拉巴州,其平均拷贝数与其他州相近。序列分析显示博尔诺州和约贝州分离出的Echovirus E19毒株之间存在遗传多样性。博尔诺州分离出的一株Echovirus E19与尼日利亚伊巴丹之前描述的一株毒株有密切关系。这些发现表明尼日利亚东北部大多数污水样本中存在多样且高水平的NPEV污染。此外,Echovirus E19与十多年前在尼日利亚西南部描述的毒株之间的相似性突显了当地活跃的传播,并强调了在One Health生态位中持续进行NPEV 监测的必要性。

title: Beyond Hesitancy: Designing Multi-Level Responses to Polio Vaccine Refusal in High-Risk Karachi, Pakistan
abstract: Abstract Pakistan remains one of the few settings in which wild poliovirus type 1 continues to circulate, and repeated vaccine refusals in high-risk communities threaten the final stages of eradication. This case study examines research conducted in three High-Risk Union Councils in Karachi, selected because they were persistent hotspots for refusals and poliovirus detection. Using the Socio-Ecological Model, the study drew on 23 in-depth interviews and 10 focus group discussions with vaccine-refusing parents, polio programme staff, physicians and government stakeholders. The findings show that refusal cannot be explained by “hesitancy” alone. At the intrapersonal level, limited knowledge, fear of side effects, infertility rumours and campaign fatigue were important. Community-level influences included household gatekeepers, language and social identity, trusted local figures and digital misinformation. Institutional barriers included weak frontline training, workload pressures, poor refusal tracking and limited physician involvement, while policy-level concerns centred on distrust of government, unmet municipal needs and the vertical structure of the polio programme. The study translated these findings into communication and operational recommendations that were subsequently discussed with provincial and national Emergency Operations Centres. The case illustrates how multi-level analysis can move vaccine refusal research towards context-specific, trust-centred programme design, while highlighting the need to evaluate whether these recommendations improve acceptance in practice. full_text: Abstract Background Non-pharmaceutical interventions (NPIs) during the COVID-19 pandemic reduced transmission of many childhood infections. Post-pandemic changes have mostly been assessed by case numbers; changes in age and seasonal distribution have received less attention. We described these changes for three notifiable childhood diseases differing in how population immunity is acquired. Methods We analysed surveillance records of hand, foot and mouth disease (HFMD), pertussis and mumps among children aged < 15 years in Haidian District, Beijing, 2015–2025. Incidence in the post-NPI (2023–2025) and pre-pandemic (2015–2019) periods was compared using quasi-Poisson regression with population denominators. Age distributions were compared using Kolmogorov–Smirnov tests, pre-pandemic trend projections and age-specific incidence, and seasonality using Watson U2 tests. Results Of 23,379 cases (HFMD 21,134; mumps 1,697; pertussis 548), pertussis incidence increased after NPI relaxation (incidence rate ratio [IRR] 9.93, 95% confidence interval 4.82–20.44), with 104 and 187 cases among children aged 6–14 years in 2023 and 2024, compared with none in 2015–2019 (pre-NPI period). HFMD incidence was lower overall (IRR 0.49, 0.35–0.69), although not after adjustment for a linear time trend, and case numbers in the first post-NPI season were within the pre-pandemic range. Incidence fell among children aged < 6 years (IRR 0.37, 0.26–0.52) and rose from 117.3 to 272.6 per 100,000 among those aged 10–14 years. The median age of HFMD cases rose from 3.55 to 6.33 years, exceeding the 95% prediction intervals of the pre-pandemic trend in 2023 and 2025, and after accounting for population change the ratio of school-age to preschool incidence increased 3.59-fold (2.06–6.28). The seasonal distribution of HFMD changed (P < 0.001). The circular mean moved from late July to late September. Mumps incidence declined similarly among preschool and school-age children (IRR 0.37 and 0.39), with no significant change in the school-age to preschool incidence ratio or seasonality. Conclusions The three diseases changed differently after NPI relaxation. For HFMD, the age distribution changed beyond the pre-pandemic trend and changes in population structure, and the seasonal distribution changed, without an increase in total incidence. Surveillance should monitor who is affected and when, not only case numbers. The causes of these changes remain undetermined. analysis.summary_en: This study investigated the incidence, age distribution and seasonality of hand, foot and mouth disease (HFMD), pertussis and mumps in children in Beijing after the relaxation of non-pharmaceutical interventions (NPIs) during the COVID-19 pandemic.
